info.title: ask
info.description: Asynchronous questions over governed data: a ticket now, a stream of structured events, an answer when there is one. The contract the agent serves; the executor contract is services/contract/openapi.json and is a different thing with a different implementer. Reached through the gateway with the USER's bearer, like every other surface.

post.summary: Open a conversation to ask within
post.description: A conversation holds the turns so a later ask can say "that team". History lives in memory for DAS_ASK_TTL_S after the last ask and is never persisted; the question text exists nowhere else in the service. A conversation with a single ask is the one-shot case and costs nothing extra.

post.summary: Ask a question; get a ticket before any tool call runs
post.description: Returns as soon as the ticket exists. The run starts after the response is sent, so a client that opens the event stream immediately sees `accepted` as seq 1 and misses nothing. One ask at a time per conversation: a second while one is running is 409.

value.question: Which support team resolves tickets fastest?
Which support team resolves tickets fastest?

202.description: Accepted; the run has not started

409.description: An ask is already running in this conversation

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last `seq` received. The stream resumes at seq+1 with no gap; 0 or absent replays from the start. The stream is lossless within DAS_ASK_TTL_S of the terminal event, except that `step` events may be dropped when the retained buffer exceeds DAS_ASK_MAX_EVENTS.

get.summary: The ticket's events, as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Each frame is `id: <seq>` and `event: <type>` with one JSON object in `data:` conforming to events.schema.json. The stream closes after `done`. A reconnect after `done` replays and closes again until the ticket expires. Keep-alive comments are sent every 15s while a run is quiet.

410.description: The ticket has expired; its events are gone

get.summary: The ticket's terminal state, for clients without SSE

post.description: Guarantees: no event but `error{kind: cancelled}` and `done` follows, and no further model call is made. Does NOT guarantee that no further tool call completes: one already in flight to the executor finishes, and its audit line exists. That is acceptable because every tool is read-only and nothing needs compensating; the contract states it rather than implies it. Idempotent; cancelling a finished ticket is 202 and changes nothing.

bearer.description: The USER's token for api://data-agent-service, validated against the tenant's JWKS exactly as the executor validates it. Every tool call the run makes carries this same token, so the sources apply this user's permissions, and a token that expires mid-run fails the next tool call rather than anything here. A ticket and a conversation belong to the `oid` that created them.

Unauthenticated.description: No bearer, or one that does not validate

NotYours.description: Not found — also the answer for a ticket or conversation that exists but belongs to another identity, so existence leaks nothing

context.description: false is the ablation: the same agent with no access to the catalog. Exists so the evals can drive this surface as they drive the library.

model.description: Overrides DAS_MODEL for this ask. Recorded in `done`.

terminal.description: The terminal event, once finished: an `answer`, `abstention`, `refusal` or `error` object from events.schema.json.
